name: The sense of 'I' (ahaṃkāra)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The sense of 'I' is listed among the constituents of the field (13.6); its absence (anahaṃkāra) is among the items called knowledge (13.9).

name: Ignorance veiling knowledge (ajñāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: what is other than the dispositions called knowledge is ignorance (13.12); tamas is born of ignorance and deludes all embodied beings (14.8); covering knowledge, tamas attaches to heedlessness (14.9); ignorance is the fruit of tamas and arises from it (14.16–17).

name: Laziness (ālasya)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Indolence is one of the three by which tamas binds (14.8).

name: Hypocrisy of the unrealised (dambha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Absence of pretence (adambhitva) is among the items called knowledge (13.8).

name: The pairs of opposites (dvandva)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The undeluded, released from the pairs known as pleasure and pain, reach the imperishable place (15.5); the one beyond the guṇas is the same in pain and pleasure, praise and blame, honour and dishonour (14.24-14.25).

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Aversion is listed among the contents of the field (13.7); the one beyond the guṇas does not hate illumination, activity and delusion when they are present (14.22).

name: Bondage by the three guṇas
description: Bhagavad Gītā 14.5–9: sattva, rajas and tamas, born of prakṛti, bind the imperishable embodied one in the body — sattva by attachment to happiness and to knowledge, rajas by attachment to action, tamas by heedlessness, idleness and sleep; attachment to the guṇas causes births in good and bad wombs (13.22).
members: sattva: attachment to happiness (sukha-saṅga) and to knowledge (jñāna-saṅga)
antidotes: seeing no agent but the guṇas and knowing what is higher than them (14.19)
serving the Lord with the unswerving yoga of devotion (14.26)

name: Desire (kāma)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Those whose desires have turned away (vinivṛtta-kāma) reach the imperishable place (15.5).

name: Greed (lobha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Greed arises when rajas has increased and comes from rajas (14.12, 14.17).

name: Pride, thinking highly of oneself (mānitva, māna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Pride, thinking highly of oneself: its absence (amānitva) heads the items called knowledge (13.8); those free from pride and delusion (nirmāna-moha) reach the imperishable place (15.5).
notes: New obstacle (extractor B) for the Gītā's māna / mānitva (13.8 amānitva, 15.5 nirmāna). Flagged for the S5 review with the existing pride obstacles, which are other traditions' (obs:mana, the Buddhist fetter of conceit; obs:mana-pride, Pāśupata; obs:abhimana, obs:abhimana-dambha).

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: tamas deludes all embodied beings (14.8); delusion arises when tamas increases and comes from it (14.13, 14.17); the one gone beyond the guṇas neither hates nor longs for it (14.22); those free of pride and delusion reach the imperishable place (15.5); the deluded (vimūḍha) do not see the living being (15.10).

name: Sleep as a bond of tamas (nidrā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Sleep is one of the three — with heedlessness and indolence — by which tamas binds the embodied one (14.8).
notes: New obstacle (extractor B): sleep as one of the three bonds of tamas (14.8). Compare obs:extremes-of-food-and-sleep (6.16) and the other traditions' obs:styana and obs:thina-middha (not the same list).

name: Heedlessness (pramāda)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Heedlessness: tamas binds by it (14.8), attaches one to it, covering knowledge (14.9); it is a sign and a product of tamas (14.13, 14.17).

name: Passion, attachment (rāga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Rajas has passion (rāga) for its nature (14.7).

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Attachment to the guṇas is the cause of births (13.22); sattva binds by attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas by attachment to action (14.6-14.7); non-attachment and not clinging are among the items called knowledge (13.10); the aśvattha is cut with the weapon of non-attachment (15.3); the fault of attachment is to be conquered (15.5).

name: The sense of 'I am the doer' (kartṛtva-abhimāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Whoever sees actions done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer sees truly (13.30); the seer sees no doer other than the guṇas (14.19).

name: Craving (tṛṣṇā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Rajas is bound up with thirst and attachment (14.7).
